evidence_chain: [Fact] Descartes’ FY2026 MD&A says the company uses technology and networks to simplify logistics and supply-chain business processes and powers supply chains through its Global Logistics Network. Source: SEC FY2026 MD&A, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050140/000110465926026450/dsgx-20260131xex99d2.htm

[Fact] FY2026 revenue was $729.0 million, up 12% year over year; services revenue was $677.2 million, or 93% of total revenue. Source: FY2026 press release filed with SEC, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050140/000092963826000965/exhibit99-1.htm

[Fact] FY2026 MD&A states that growth from new and existing customers was driven by global trade intelligence and transportation management solutions; FY2025 growth from new and existing customers was driven by global trade intelligence, routing, and transportation management solutions. Source: SEC FY2026 MD&A, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050140/000110465926026450/dsgx-20260131xex99d2.htm

[Fact] Descartes acquired Finale on August 1, 2025; the company describes Finale as cloud-based inventory management software designed to support ecommerce businesses across their growth lifecycle. Source: SEC FY2026 MD&A, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050140/000110465926026450/dsgx-20260131xex99d2.htm

[Fact] Descartes acquired OrderMine on March 11, 2026; the company describes OrderMine as AI-powered forecasting and demand-planning solutions designed to support ecommerce businesses across their growth lifecycle. Source: SEC FY2026 MD&A, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050140/000110465926026450/dsgx-20260131xex99d2.htm

[Fact] In Q2 FY2026, management said customers faced uncertainty in sourcing and moving goods across borders and that the Global Logistics Network is relied on by shippers, carriers, and logistics service providers to keep goods moving. Source: Descartes Q2 FY2026 results, https://www.descartes.com/resources/news/descartes-announces-fiscal-2026-second-quarter-financial-results?language=en

[Fact] As of June 11, 2026, DSGX market capitalization from the finance tool was approximately $6.3 billion, placing it in the requested USD 300M-10B underfollowed small/mid-cap discovery range. Source: finance tool snapshot for DSGX, latest trade time 2026-06-11 11:25:02 UTC.
[Inference] High services revenue mix supports a recurring/network-like business model, but the evidence reviewed does not prove high retail/ecommerce revenue purity.

[Inference] Ecommerce-oriented acquisitions increase the plausibility of consumer-supply-chain exposure, but acquisition size and contribution must be measured before treating this as a primary growth driver.
[Hypothesis] Tariff, customs, and cross-border complexity could increase usage, retention, or pricing power for DSGX tools if retail and ecommerce customers rely on them in daily shipment execution.
falsification_plan: Falsify if annual filings, investor materials, or management commentary show retail, ecommerce, CPG, wholesale, or consumer-goods customers are immaterial to revenue or growth.
Falsify if organic growth from new and existing customers slows while reported growth is sustained mainly by acquisitions.

Falsify if global trade intelligence, routing, transportation management, ecommerce inventory/order management, or customs-compliance products show weak organic demand despite tariff/customs complexity.
Falsify if customer case studies show DSGX used mainly by generic freight/logistics intermediaries with no meaningful consumer retail fulfillment linkage.
Falsify if churn, retention, or pricing disclosures indicate customers treat DSGX as substitutable software rather than embedded network infrastructure.
Falsify if tariff/customs volatility causes customer purchasing delays without later conversion into higher recurring usage, expansion, or retention.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: Quantify how much DSGX revenue and organic growth is tied to retail, ecommerce, consumer goods, wholesale, parcel, marketplace, 3PL, customs broker, and carrier workflows versus non-retail industrial/logistics verticals. The most important hidden signal is not whether DSGX sells generic logistics software, but whether consumer-facing supply chains generate material recurring usage across customs, routing, inventory, order, transportation management, and ecommerce fulfillment workflows.
next_research_tasks: Pull the FY2026 Annual Information Form and investor presentation to search for customer verticals, retail/ecommerce references, segment language, and any disclosed end-market mix.
Build a revenue bridge separating organic growth, acquisition contribution, services revenue, professional services, and license revenue for FY2024-FY2026 and latest quarters.
Search Descartes case studies for named or anonymized retailers, ecommerce merchants, marketplaces, CPG brands, wholesalers, 3PLs, customs brokers, parcel carriers, and omnichannel distributors.

Map acquired assets since FY2024 into consumer relevance buckets: ecommerce inventory/order management, shipping, demand planning, routing, last-mile, customs compliance, carrier safety, and non-consumer logistics.
Review earnings-call transcripts for management comments on tariffs, de minimis, customs filings, parcel volumes, ecommerce, retail, CPG, wholesale, and organic growth.

Compare DSGX against reference leaders and substitutes such as large ERP/TMS vendors, parcel software platforms, customs brokerage systems, and marketplace-owned fulfillment stacks to test defensibility.

Track KPIs that would upgrade the thesis: disclosed retail/ecommerce customer wins, expansion in customs/trade-compliance usage, recurring revenue retention, organic services growth, transaction/network volume metrics, and evidence that ecommerce acquisitions are cross-sold into GLN customers.

Track KPIs that would downgrade the thesis: acquisition-led revenue without organic acceleration, declining shipment/import-related demand, margin pressure from integration, or lack of consumer-vertical disclosure after repeated investor questions.
risks: [Purity risk] Retail, ecommerce, CPG, and wholesale exposure may be too small relative to broader logistics, manufacturing, freight, broker, government, or industrial customers.
[Acquisition-quality risk] Reported growth may depend heavily on acquisitions rather than organic network usage, pricing power, or same-customer expansion.
[Substitutability risk] Customers may view individual DSGX modules as replaceable point tools rather than deeply embedded workflow infrastructure.
[Cycle risk] Consumer demand softness, lower import volumes, destocking, or weaker parcel/shipping activity could reduce usage growth even if compliance complexity rises.
[Integration risk] Recent and future acquisitions may dilute margins, complicate product integration, or obscure organic performance.

[Competitive risk] Large enterprise software vendors, TMS providers, parcel platforms, customs brokers’ internal systems, marketplace logistics stacks, and private-equity-backed shipping software platforms could limit pricing power.
[Evidence risk] Current disclosures do not provide a clean vertical revenue split, making the consumer thesis vulnerable to over-attribution.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Consumer demand node: retail, ecommerce, marketplaces, brands, CPG, wholesale distributors. Execution layer: 3PLs, freight forwarders, parcel carriers, customs brokers, warehouse/fulfillment operators. DSGX position: network and software layer for logistics-intensive businesses, including GLN connectivity, trade intelligence, customs and regulatory compliance, transportation management, routing, inventory/order management, ecommerce shipping and forecasting/demand-planning acquisitions. Chokepoint logic: shipment execution and cross-border compliance require reliable data exchange among shippers, carriers, brokers, government agencies, and fulfillment partners; replacing embedded logistics/compliance workflows may create operational risk.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: DSGX 不是直接消费品牌，而是消费供应链后台基础设施候选。若零售商、电商平台、品牌商、批发商和 3PL 面对更复杂的关税、海关申报、跨境运输、路由、库存和末端交付要求，Descartes 的 Global Logistics Network、全球贸易智能、运输管理、海关/监管合规、库存管理和电商履约相关工具可能成为难以绕开的工作流层。当前不能把它定性为高纯度消费标的，因为公开证据尚未量化零售、电商、CPG、批发客户收入占比；它仍应被保留为“消费相邻基础设施”深挖对象。
deep_reports.thesis_en: [Hypothesis] DSGX is not a direct consumer brand but a consumer-supply-chain infrastructure candidate. If retailers, ecommerce merchants, brands, wholesalers, and 3PLs face greater tariff, customs, cross-border shipment, routing, inventory, and last-mile complexity, Descartes’ Global Logistics Network, global trade intelligence, transportation management, customs/regulatory compliance, inventory management, and ecommerce-fulfillment tools may become embedded workflow infrastructure. The thesis is not yet high-purity because public evidence reviewed so far does not quantify revenue from retail, ecommerce, CPG, or wholesale customers. DSGX should remain in the funnel as an adjacent consumer-infrastructure target pending vertical-exposure verification.

deep_reports.why_underfollowed: DSGX is commonly screened as logistics software, supply-chain software, or trade-compliance software rather than as a Consumer theme company. That can cause consumer investors to miss its second-order exposure to retail/ecommerce shipment execution, customs filing, parcel visibility, routing, inventory flow, and cross-border fulfillment. The market may also focus on DSGX as an acquisition-driven software compounder and overlook whether its network layer is becoming more important as tariffs, de minimis changes, customs rules, nearshoring, and omnichannel retail complexity increase.

memory_update.reason: Supported as a logistics/trade-compliance network company with ecommerce-adjacent acquisitions and high services revenue mix, but consumer vertical exposure remains unquantified.

memory_update.gap: Need quantified retail, ecommerce, CPG, wholesale, and consumer-goods revenue or customer evidence before upgrading from adjacent infrastructure hypothesis to core Consumer theme candidate.

memory_update.trigger: Material retail/ecommerce/CPG/wholesale exposure plus evidence of organic growth from trade compliance, transportation management, routing, ecommerce inventory, or fulfillment workflows.
Evidence that growth is acquisition-led, consumer vertical exposure is immaterial, or DSGX products are replaceable point tools rather than embedded workflow/network infrastructure.

summary: Layer 5 mini deep report for DSGX under the Consumer theme. Conclusion: keep DSGX in the underfollowed lane as a consumer-adjacent infrastructure hypothesis, not yet a high-purity consumer exposure. The strongest supported facts are that Descartes operates the Global Logistics Network for logistics-intensive businesses, has high services revenue mix, serves shippers/carriers/logistics service providers, and has added ecommerce-oriented assets such as Finale and OrderMine. The main unresolved issue is customer-vertical purity: current evidence does not quantify retail, ecommerce, wholesale, or consumer-goods revenue contribution. Upgrade requires filings, investor materials, or customer evidence showing material consumer-supply-chain exposure and organic growth tied to trade-compliance, routing, inventory, ecommerce fulfillment, or parcel workflows.
